around.headline: Traffic curbs across Bengaluru for new Cabinet ministers' swearing-in
around.summary: Karnataka's Cabinet expansion — 20 new ministers — was sworn in today at Lok Bhavan, and police put traffic restrictions in place around the venue. If your route passes near Vidhana Soudha/Lok Bhavan this evening, expect diversions and add extra travel time.
around.source: The Hindu, Deccan Herald, The News Minute

around.headline: Night trains resume on Bengaluru–Mangaluru–Kozhikode route
around.summary: Night train services on the Bengaluru–Mangaluru–Kozhikode route restart from today, August 3. If you're booked on this route, plan your overnight travel again — but check PNR/running status given recent weather-linked rail disruptions in the region.

around.headline: Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway toll hiked
around.summary: Toll rates on the Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway have gone up. If you're driving that route, budget for the new rates before you set off.

around.headline: Bengaluru just had its second-driest July in 108 years
around.summary: A faltering monsoon left the city with its second-driest July on record. Expect continued pressure on water supply this year — a good prompt to keep conserving even during rainy spells like tonight's.

around.headline: New traffic model eases congestion in east Bengaluru — without new roads
around.summary: A revamped traffic-management approach has cut congestion in parts of east Bengaluru without any road widening. Commuters on affected corridors may notice smoother flow starting now.

around.headline: Floods and heavy rain kill 14, displace thousands across southern India
around.summary: Rains and flooding have killed at least 14 people and displaced thousands across southern India this week. With Bengaluru itself facing a 78% rain chance today, avoid known waterlogging spots and keep emergency contacts handy.

street_smart.title: You flag down an auto for a short ride and the driver agrees — but halfway there, he stops and says the fare just doubled, or you can get out right there.
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen rotation topic (auto/cab overcharging & refusal) — no matching real incident in today's feeds. Recent street-smart topics (godman/black-magic fraud, two-wheeler theft, moral-policing mobs, fake currency, a TTE's UPI fare scam, a delivery agent's home-entry request, tenant/landlord rights, phone-theft-linked bank fraud, SIR-related impersonation, and consumer court basics) have all run within the last 3 weeks; auto/cab overcharging last appeared on July 10, outside that window.
street_smart.situation: There's no meter running and no app involved — just a verbal price you agreed to before boarding. He's stopped the auto in the middle of the road, traffic is building up behind you, and he says he'll only continue (or let you out) once you agree to the new number. What do you do?

choices.text: Pay whatever he now demands so you can get moving and avoid a scene.
choices.feedback: Risky. Paying whatever's demanded teaches the driver — and anyone watching — that a mid-ride threat works, which is exactly why the same trick gets repeated on the next passenger.

choices.text: Refuse to pay anything at all and walk off since he broke the agreed deal.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. You did travel part of the distance, so walking off without paying anything leaves you legally in the wrong too — the driver can (and sometimes does) call this in as a fare dodge. It also documents nothing about the actual overcharging attempt, so nothing changes for the next passenger.

choices.text: Calmly hold your ground: agree to pay only the fare you originally settled on, note the auto's registration number and take a photo, and tell him you'll file a complaint with Bengaluru Traffic Police if he won't honour it.
choices.feedback: Correct. A mid-ride fare hike is a pressure tactic that works only if you look rattled — a driver who's bluffing usually backs down once he sees you calmly noting his registration number instead of panicking. If he still won't honour the agreed fare, that registration number is exactly what you need to file a complaint with Bengaluru Traffic Police or through a ride app's fare-dispute option.

choices.text: Loudly threaten to call the police and create a scene right there on the road.
choices.feedback: Risky. A shouting match on a public street can escalate fast and puts you at more physical risk than the fare dispute is worth — a calm, documented response protects you better than confrontation.

takeaways: Before boarding any auto, confirm upfront whether it's 'by meter' or a fixed fare — a driver who refuses to state either, or refuses the ride once you name your destination, can be reported to Bengaluru Traffic Police.
Photograph the auto's registration number/plate before or during the ride if anything about the fare feels off — it costs two seconds and is your strongest evidence if you need to complain later.

For app-based cabs and autos, always pay the fare shown in-app — never a cash 'adjustment' the driver asks for outside the app — and use the app's in-ride support/SOS option to flag disputes immediately.

quiz.question: Per today's news, how many new ministers did Congress name in Karnataka's Cabinet expansion, which brought traffic curbs to Bengaluru today?
quiz.why: Cabinet reshuffles often trigger short-term traffic restrictions near swearing-in venues like Lok Bhavan, since routes need to be secured for VIP movement.

quiz.question: According to today's report, Bengaluru just recorded its second-driest ___ in 108 years.
quiz.why: Long-running weather records like this one go back to the early 1900s, letting meteorologists make century-long comparisons for Indian cities.

quiz.question: Per today's Reuters report, how many people have died so far as heavy rain and flooding struck southern India?
quiz.why: Peninsular India's hilly terrain and short, steep rivers make flash floods and landslides a recurring monsoon risk, distinct from the slower plains-style river flooding seen up north.

quiz.question: The Cauvery river, whose sharing dispute came up again in today's news, originates in which Karnataka district?
quiz.why: The river originates at Talakaveri in Kodagu district and flows over 800 km through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu before reaching the Bay of Bengal.

quiz.question: At full strength, how many elected members does India's Lok Sabha have?
quiz.why: The Rajya Sabha, India's upper house, is composed differently — up to 245 members, most elected by state legislatures rather than directly by voters.
